rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil (2x WTI)
positions.catalyst: The Hormuz crisis escalated from a scare into formal US policy overnight. Trump announced he is reinstating a naval blockade of Iranian ports AND imposing a 20% fee on ALL cargo shipped through the Strait of Hormuz; US forces struck 80+ targets inside Iran over the weekend and Iran's IRGC responded by closing the strait again. The physical evidence: roughly 230 loaded crude tankers are now stranded inside the Gulf with nowhere to deliver, and chartering a tanker from inside the strait costs $8-10m versus $4-5m from outside. Crude repriced hard on the announcement — Brent +4.45% to ~$87.01, WTI +3.3% to ~$80.75 (Reuters/Yahoo Finance, this morning). This is the second consecutive escalation step, and the first one that is a declared government action rather than a headline risk.
positions.driver: Holding the crude trade because the catalyst got STRONGER, not weaker, and the right tail is still unpriced. A 20% tariff plus a blockade applied to the waterway carrying ~20% of global crude is a supply shock, and Brent at $87 still prices a disruption, not a closure — a genuine sustained closure is a $100-150 Brent event, so the upside remains a multiple of the downside. The left tail is bounded and identifiable: a ceasefire/deal headline takes crude back toward the pre-escalation ~$73-78 shelf, roughly -8-10% on the underlying, and no de-escalation sends oil to zero. Crucially this is again the only pick on the board uncorrelated to today's three equity coin-flips — June CPI at 8:30 ET, Warsh's first Congressional testimony at 10:00, and JPM/BAC earnings — and it is the one asset that RISES if oil-driven inflation sours all three (Bloomberg: 'Stocks, Bonds Fall as Oil Jump Fuels Fed-Hike Bets'). WTI over Brent because 2x leverage on WTI's +3.3% out-torques 1x Brent's +4.45%, and a Hormuz tax structurally bids US landlocked barrels as the safe alternative supply. RUNNERS-UP: BNO (1x Brent) rejected — purest transmission of a seaborne Gulf disruption and it is outperforming WTI, but unleveraged it delivers too little torque on a high-conviction catalyst. SOXL (3x semis) rejected outright — it is +8.9% pre-market on an SK Hynix/memory bounce (SOX ETF only +2.4%), squarely inside the no-chase band, and a one-day dead-cat bounce in a sector that just got routed is the worst possible thing to buy at 3x. FRO/DHT/TNK (tankers) rejected — the obvious beneficiary, but they are only +1-2% pre-market despite the blockade, the setup is ambiguous for owners (rates spike but 230 vessels are trapped and volumes collapse), the group is already +60% YTD, and Evercore just downgraded DHT/FRO/NAT on 'reversion risk'. BOIL/UNG (natgas) rejected — Qatari LNG is also trapped, but Henry Hub is domestically set and the tape agrees: natgas is FLAT to -0.6% today, so the transmission is not there. UGL/NUGT (gold) rejected — the right hedge but only +1.3-1.4%; too little payoff for an all-in book.
positions.risks: This is a war trade and I am now holding it into an extended move: WTI is already +3.3% and Brent +4.45% this morning, so I am buying strength, and there is a live competing narrative that an Iran deal could 'reset the market.' A ceasefire, hostage deal, or credible Iranian climb-down gaps crude down hard overnight before we can act, and at 2x that is doubled — that is the explicit price of the convexity. Leverage stays at 2x rather than 3x-equivalent precisely because the catalyst is headline-driven, two-way, and now partially priced. Secondary risks: OPEC+ spare capacity outside the Gulf is the natural brake on any spike; UCO is futures-based so roll/contango decay exists but is immaterial over a 24h hold. Hard stop 35.82 (-8% on the 2x, i.e. ~-4% on WTI), set below the pre-blockade WTI shelf so it triggers on genuine de-escalation and not on intraday chop. PRICE-QUALITY FLAG for this run: UCO's pre-market book is thin and lagging — it quotes 38.80/38.93 (+0.2%) while USO is +2.2% and WTI futures are +3.3%, i.e. the leveraged ETF has not repriced pre-open. Both the dashboard proxy (38.74, asOf 2026-07-14T11:40:57Z) and Robinhood (bid 38.80 / ask 38.93, 11:40:39Z) agree on this level, so the book is marked consistently at it: the UCO exit was taken at the live 38.80 bid and the re-entry at the live 38.93 ask. This makes the accounting effectively close-to-close and internally consistent with Monday's entry, which was struck the same way — no phantom gain is booked; today's crude move will be captured on tomorrow's exit.
